rv.q: It all makes for an experience that’s rich, challenging, and well worth pondering long after it ends.
Raven Theatre’s production of Martyna Majok’s Ironbound directed by Georgette Verdin is a brilliantly patient drama supported by a stellar cast and a detail-oriented creative team.
Carapetyan's performance is one for the ages: it ought to be remembered at Jeff Award time.
Raven Theater’s polished production of IRONBOUND will definitely help make Martyna Majok a household name.
It’s a sharp, poignant production, full of dark humor and real heart.
Director Verdin does a superb job of keeping the action brisk and the mood from degenerating into tragedy even as it explores issues such as immigration, domestic violence, and the working poor.

cn.t: Critics praise Majok's immigrant drama for brilliant writing and a tour-de-force lead performance by Lucy Carapetyan, though the story itself is a downer that examines the harsh realities of working-class immigrant life.
